message.content:
In /bench/repo (the memos Go repo), investigate with thoroughness "very thorough" and report exact file paths and line numbers:

A) Markdown processing: internal/markdown likely defines an interface (e.g. Service or Parser). Report the interface name and path:line, the concrete implementation(s) (e.g. goldmark-based), who constructs them (constructor call sites in production code — server setup, store, api service), and which components/structs hold the interface as a field. Cite all path:line.

B) Memo derived metadata: memos have a computed "payload" or "snippet"/property (tags, hasLink, hasTaskList, hasCode, hasIncompleteTasks, snippet) computed from content. Find where it's computed (e.g. memo_payload.go RebuildMemoPayload or similar in server/router/api/v1 or store), which operations trigger recomputation (CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, others? maybe a migrator/runner), and exactly what properties are extracted. Cite path:line for the computation function and each trigger call site.

C) Fan-in aggregation: among functions/methods declared under internal/, which has the highest number of inbound calls across the repo? Check candidates like internal/util functions (util.GenUUID, util.ValidateEmail?), internal/base, internal/markdown helpers. Use grep to count call sites of top candidates (e.g. `grep -rn "util\.[A-Z][A-Za-z]*(" --include=*.go | grep -v _test` and tally). Report the winner symbol, its declaration path:line, and approximate caller count (non-test and total).

D) Entity reference breadth: among store entity types (store.Memo, store.User, store.Attachment/Resource, store.Activity, store.Reaction, etc. defined in store/*.go), which is referenced from the most distinct packages OUTSIDE the store layer (i.e. outside store/ and store/db/)? Count distinct package directories referencing `store.User` vs `store.Memo` vs others via grep. Report top two with rough package counts.

Report facts with path:line citations, concise.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Findings below (all paths absolute).

## A) Markdown processing

**Interface**: `markdown.Service` — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`
Methods (declared at): `ExtractAll` :33, `ExtractTags` :36, `ExtractProperties` :39, `RenderMarkdown` :42, `RenderHTML` :45, `GenerateSnippet` :48, `ValidateContent` :51, `RenameTag` :54.
Helper type `markdown.ExtractedData{Tags, Mentions, Property}` — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:21`.

**Concrete impl** (single, goldmark-based): unexported `service struct { md goldmark.Markdown }` — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:58`. Method impls at :143 (ExtractTags), :193 (ExtractProperties), :244 (RenderMarkdown), :255 (RenderHTML), :264 (GenerateSnippet), :349 (ValidateContent), :356 (ExtractAll), :425 (RenameTag).

**Constructor**: `markdown.NewService(opts ...Option) Service` — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:85`, with options `WithTagExtension` :71 and `WithMentionExtension` :78 (goldmark extenders: `extension.GFM` plus `extensions.TagExtension` `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/extensions/tag.go:14` and `extensions.MentionExtension` `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/extensions/mention.go:14`).

**Construction call sites (production)** — exactly one:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-50` inside `NewAPIV1Service` (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:47`), assigned at `:56`.
Test-only constructions: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`, `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss_test.go:54`, `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go:427`.

**Structs holding the interface as a field**:
- `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`
- `rss.RSSService.MarkdownService` — `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:45` (constructed `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:58`, wired from the API service instance at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:85`)
- `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16` (constructor `NewRunner` at `:19`) — **note: `memopayload.NewRunner` has zero call sites anywhere in the repo** (only `s3presign.NewRunner` is started, `/bench/repo/server/server.go:162`), so `Runner`/`RunOnce` is currently dead code.

**Interface method consumers**:
- `ExtractAll`: `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:80`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32` (`resolveMentionTargets`)
- `GenerateSnippet`: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:85` (`getMemoContentSnippet`, decl :83)
- `RenderHTML`: `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:339` (`getRSSItemDescription`)
- `ExtractTags`, `ExtractProperties`, `RenderMarkdown`, `ValidateContent`, `RenameTag`: **no production callers** (test-only / unused).

## B) Memo derived metadata

**Computation function**: `RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error` — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`. It calls `markdownService.ExtractAll` (:80) and assigns `memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags` (:85) and `memo.Payload.Property = data.Property` (:86). Note it does not clear stale fields other than these two.

**Actual property extraction** happens in `service.ExtractAll` — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`:
- tags from `mast.TagNode` :376-378 (deduped, case-preserved, :418; `uniquePreserveCase` :456); tag nodes inside links/images are skipped (`isTagNodeInLinkOrImage` :122, `asMemoTagNode` :134)
- mentions from `mast.MentionNode`, lowercased :379-381
- `Property.Title` from a leading H1 :384-389
- `Property.HasLink` :394 (`gast.KindLink`)
- `Property.HasCode` :397 (`KindCodeBlock`, `KindFencedCodeBlock`, `KindCodeSpan`)
- `Property.HasTaskList` :400 and `Property.HasIncompleteTasks` :403 (unchecked `east.TaskCheckBox`)

Proto definition of the property set: `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto:15-23` (`has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title`); generated struct `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go:85-93`. `tags` is `MemoPayload.tags` (`/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto:12`).

**Trigger call sites of `RebuildMemoPayload`** (only 3 total, 2 reachable):
1. `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` — inside `CreateMemo` (decl `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70`), before `s.Store.CreateMemo` at :115
2. `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447` — inside `UpdateMemo` (decl :401), only on the `content` update-mask path; sets `update.Content`/`update.Payload` :449-450, persisted at :496
3. `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52` — batch backfill in `Runner.RunOnce` (decl :27, batch size 100), which is **never invoked** (no `memopayload.NewRunner` caller; `/bench/repo/store/migrator.go` does not touch payloads either)

Other memo writes deliberately do not recompute: `touchMemoUpdatedTimestamp` `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:16-24`, and the non-content branches of `UpdateMemo`.

**Snippet is NOT stored in the payload** — it is computed on the fly at response-conversion time via `getMemoContentSnippet` (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83`, maxLength 64). Callers:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:76` (per-memo conversion, assigned :80)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:225` and `:248` (`batchConvertMemoRelations`, decl :173)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:154`, `:162`
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:323` (`memoNotificationSnippet`, decl :318; used at :346, :350, :374, :387)

Payload consumers: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:48-50` (+`convertMemoPropertyFromStore` :315) and stats aggregation `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:138-152` and `:254-268`.

## C) Fan-in aggregation (functions declared under internal/)

**Winner: `util.GenUUID`** — declared `/bench/repo/internal/util/util.go:40`.
- 28 call sites total, 7 non-test, across 9 files.
- Non-test callers: `/bench/repo/server/auth/token.go:194`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/auth_service_session.go:26` and `:135`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_storage.go:209`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:154`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sso_username.go:15`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_access_tokens.go:84`.

Runners-up (total qualified call sites, repo-wide incl. tests):
- `filter.DefaultEngine` — 7 (`/bench/repo/internal/filter/engine.go`), used by store/db dialect files
- `util.ConvertStringToInt32` — 5 total / 5 non-test (`/bench/repo/internal/util/util.go:14`)
- `version.IsVersionGreaterThan` — 4 (`/bench/repo/internal/version/version.go`)
- `filter.DefaultAttachmentEngine` — 4
- `markdown.Service` methods: `ExtractAll` 2, `GenerateSnippet` 1, `RenderHTML` 1 non-test

Package-level totals of qualified calls: `util` 37, `scheduler` 31 (all self-referential in its own external tests/doc.go — no production consumers), `filter` 17, `webhook` 9, `version` 9, `markdown` 9, `base` 3, `motionphoto` 2.
Dead in `internal/util`: `HasPrefixes` (:23), `ValidateEmail` (:33), `ReplaceString` (:66) — 0 call sites outside the package.

## D) Entity reference breadth

Counting distinct package directories referencing each type, excluding `store/` and `store/db/`:

1. **`store.User`** (declared `/bench/repo/store/user.go`) — **7 distinct outside packages**, 119 total reference lines repo-wide:
`server/router/api/v1` (19 files), `server/router/api/v1/test` (3), `server/router/rss` (2), `server/router/fileserver` (2), `server/auth` (2), `server/router/frontend` (1), `server/notification` (1).
2. **`store.Memo`** (declared `/bench/repo/store/memo.go`) — **6 distinct outside packages**, 150 total reference lines (highest raw count):
`server/router/api/v1` (13 files), `server/router/api/v1/test` (3), `server/router/rss` (2), `server/runner/memopayload` (1), `server/router/frontend` (1), `server/notification` (1).

Next tier: `store.Attachment` 8 dirs incl. store layer (97 refs), `store.Inbox` 7 dirs (57), `store.MemoRelation` 7 dirs (53), `store.Reaction` 6 dirs (40), `store.IdentityProvider` 4 (26), `store.UserSetting` 4 (23). `store.Shortcut`, `store.Activity`, `store.MemoOrganizer`, `store.WorkspaceSetting` have 0 references outside the store layer.

Summary: `store.User` has the broadest package fan-out; `store.Memo` has the most raw references but is confined to one fewer package.
